principles.statement: Model interaction as a distinct capability from monologic speaking; do not infer conversational ability from isolated oral production scores alone.
Require learner responses to be contingent on actual preceding turns and record response relevance separately from grammar, pronunciation and fluency.
Use an appropriate next turn as comprehension evidence when possible; fall back to explicit listening diagnostics only when interaction does not provide interpretable evidence.
Teach turn-taking, listener support and sequence progression inside short goal-driven exchanges rather than as decontextualized conversation tips.
Treat learner-initiated clarification and repair as positive interactional strategies when they restore shared understanding and allow the task to progress.
Do not reward fake comprehension by penalizing every clarification request; interpret repair frequency together with source-turn difficulty and repair success.
Progress near-A0 interaction through bounded shared goals and increasing turn/wording/partner variability rather than through unstructured open chat from the start.
Teach pragmatic language as form plus social function plus context plus sequence position; do not reduce pragmatics to isolated polite phrases.
Prioritize high-frequency survival functions—greeting/closing, request, accept/decline, apology, permission, clarification and confirmation—then test them in changed contexts.
Protect interaction progressivity: repair meaning-blocking problems during the exchange, but defer many non-blocking form corrections until a task boundary.
Use AI/chatbots as scalable rehearsal partners, not as proof of real-world interaction capability; require changed-partner and human-calibrated transfer evidence for stronger claims.

Record how much the partner repeats, rephrases, supplies language, leads the exchange or silently infers ambiguous learner intent, because partner rescue changes the evidential value of task completion.
Do not treat ASR success or LLM semantic inference as human intelligibility evidence; distinguish machine recognition, model intent inference and human listener understanding.

Calibrate automated interaction judgments—including response contingency, pragmatic fit, intelligibility and repair classification—against stratified human judgments before using them for mastery decisions.

Prefer low-inference observable interaction evidence such as relevant next turns, goal completion and successful repair over opaque holistic scores such as naturalness or conversation ability percentages.

Keep turn-count progression, latency expectations, repair frequency, pragmatic syllabus, AI accommodation, partner-rescue thresholds, automated scoring and human-transfer criteria falsifiable until EXP-015 validates them for Vietnamese near-A0 learners.
